You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto loan applications down. Lending volume index: 79.
People around you are stressed: Rick Tanner. The mood is tense.

The Millfield Community Credit Union phone call from tick 11 finally produced a live signal: the small business lending manager scheduled a 20-minute exploratory call with David Chen for next week — not a job interview, but a real conversation with a named contact. Chen marked the lead warm and prepared the three-minute disruption-period pitch around the SBA credential. He completed four focused study sessions pushing the coursework from 75% to 90%, and sent two targeted outreach messages — one to a regional CDFI active in Millfield and one to a community development bank that had publicly engaged with the auto sector contraction — each leading with the scenario modeling work and naming the credential explicitly. He also sent Linda Park the three-scenario auto loan contraction document; she responded positively and offered to share her policy cancellation data in return, sustaining the peer exchange relationship.
